significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that an internal "information-source" direction causally modulates certainty, that its effect is ordered by evidential obligatoriness, and that source marking in one language predicts later certainty and answers in another; the latter two are form-(iii) relations, supplemented by a form-(ii) causal mechanism. This would constrain expectations across evidential conditions and language types more sharply than the topic-default hypothesis of generally shared multilingual representations, while bearing directly on shared-concept accounts such as Wendler et al.'s 2024 "Do Llamas Work in English?" rather than merely showing decodability. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—"hearsay-marked premise[s] given in Turkish" lowering English-side certainty—and a causal mechanism through the source direction; the determinate negative branch would reject the predicted ordering or leakage and support compartmentalization, although failure of only one of the three linked assertions would not settle the others. In the topic-substitution check, replacing these specific predictions with only the broad multilingual-representation topic would not retain this score, because the obligatoriness ordering and cross-language predictive coupling are the above-median contribution.

reach.justification: The transferable handles named by the claim are the "shared source direction," an evidential-obligatoriness-versus-certainty relation, and an intervention that can "ablate the direction to remove cross-lingual leakage." The intervention can act ex ante—after processing a marked premise but before producing the downstream answer—although the proposed certainty and leakage measurements are otherwise mainly post-hoc diagnostics. The vector itself would require re-extraction in each model, but the substantive ordering predicts that obligatory-evidential languages will show stronger certainty coupling and that a source-language signal can persist into target-language processing, so some conclusion survives recalibration across multilingual models and language classes; likely downstream users are primarily interpretability and model-auditing researchers rather than non-AI practitioners. The topic-substitution check lowers no further: the generic topic would supply neither this source-sensitive audit nor the pre-output steering handle, which are specific to this claim and satisfy the higher-band lead-time and relation-transfer tie-breaks.
